Definition: Integration of health records, patient registration, immunization data, and health insurance into data exchange
Comments: The eGabon CI-SIS (Clinical Information System Interoperability Framework) was developed under the eGabon-SIS project (launched 2016). A Strategic Master Plan for the National Health Information System (SDSSIS, 2017) and an eHealth interoperability framework were developed, including use cases for patient admission, laboratory, imaging, health surveillance, and patient identifier (ISG). The project reached a pilot phase by 2021. The CNAM-GS (National Health Insurance and Social Security Fund) is a major data system. Full integration with the broader government data exchange layer is not confirmed.
revision_notes: Original score (3, Under development, 2021) rested on the 2021 eGabon CI-SIS conference presentation and the 2021 Digital Gabon Project PAD, both fetched and confirmed relevant to the eHealth interoperability framework and pilot phase, but dated. Searched for fresher evidence: the SIS Phase 1 pilot went live in two hospitals (HIAOBO, HCEG) between December 2023 and December 2024, Phase 2 is expanding to eight further hospitals through 2025, and DHIS2 was launched nationally in December 2024 (TechAfrica News, Gabonreview, HISP Rwanda). Crucially, the World Bank's own Digital Gabon Project Implementation Status Report (P175987, archived 29-Jun-2024) shows the PDO indicator 'government entities actively and securely exchanging data on the government interoperability platform' at 0 actual as of June 2024 against a target of 5 by 2026, confirming that integration of health data into the cross-government data exchange remains under development rather than partially achieved. Score of 3 confirmed with updated evidence; year moved to 2025 to reflect the newest supporting sources.
revised_comments: Gabon's national Health Information System (SIS), delivered under the eGabon-SIS programme, is under active development rather than fully integrated into the government-wide data exchange. Following the 2017 Strategic Master Plan (SDSSIS) and the CI-SIS interoperability framework (first version 2019), Phase 1 of the SIS was deployed to two pilot hospitals (Hopital d'Instruction des Armees Omar Bongo Ondimba and the Hopital de la Cooperation Egypto-Gabonaise) from December 2023, with provisional handover in December 2024. Phase 2, launched in 2025, extends the system to eight further hospitals, alongside the national rollout of the DHIS2 platform (December 2024) supported by WHO Gabon, the Global Fund and CERMEL. The CNAM-GS remains the principal health insurance data system. However, the World Bank's Digital Gabon Project records zero government entities actively and securely exchanging data on the national interoperability platform as at June 2024 (against a target of five by 2026), indicating that formal integration of health data into the cross-government data exchange has not yet been achieved.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Gabon has strong infrastructure: 94% of population covered by 3G/4G (ARCEP/GSMA 2020), 1.919 million Internet subscribers (June 2020), and a national fiber-optic backbone of 1,030 km. However, the World Bank Digital Gabon Project ISR explicitly targets a rural-to-overall NIP coverage ratio of 1.0 (baseline 0.0), acknowledging a rural-urban gap. The World Bank DE4A diagnostic notes persistent digital exclusion in rural areas.
revision_notes: Original score (2, Partial rural coverage, 2020) cited a 2021 World Bank project concept note and the 2024 Digital Gabon Project ISR; both fetched and confirmed relevant. The ISR confirms a rural-to-overall NIP coverage ratio target of 1.0 from a 2020 baseline of 0, with no actual value yet posted, consistent with an unresolved urban-rural gap. Searched for fresher connectivity data: ARCEP reports 97% national telephony/internet coverage in 2024, but around 1,253 villages (approximately 117,600 people, about 6.5% of the population) remained uncovered as of February 2024, with an active Phase 2 Universal Service rollout (targeting roughly 200 additional villages across all nine provinces) still being deployed through mid-2025. This confirms 'Partial rural coverage' (2) remains the correct score; full urban-rural parity is not yet supported by the evidence. Year updated to 2024 to reflect the most recent ARCEP coverage figures underpinning the score.
revised_comments: Gabon has achieved high overall mobile broadband coverage, reaching around 97% of the national territory in 2024 according to ARCEP, with over 2 million internet and mobile subscribers, roughly matching total population. Nonetheless, a residual rural connectivity gap persists: as of February 2024, ARCEP reported some 1,253 villages (about 117,600 people, roughly 6.5% of the population) without mobile or internet coverage. The second phase of the Universal Electronic Communications Service programme, run with Airtel Gabon and Moov Africa Gabon Telecom and funded by a sector levy, is extending coverage to around 200 additional villages across all nine provinces, with site identification and radio-station deployment missions ongoing through 2025. The World Bank's Digital Gabon Project also tracks a rural-to-overall coverage ratio for the national identity number, targeting parity (a ratio of 1.0) by 2026 from a 2020 baseline of zero, reflecting the persistent urban-rural divide the project is designed to close. Rural coverage therefore remains partial rather than equitable with urban areas.
